elements.element: Customer is not required to pay liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4.2 affirmatively requires PB to pay an early-termination fee and expressly provides that the amount may be characterized as liquidated damages.

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay contractual penalties.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not separately impose an amount denominated as a penalty, and the revised Section 14.4.2 overrides the retained 300% and 25%-interest termination formulas with a single capped fee.

elements.element: Any permitted liquidated amount payable by Customer is structured as an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4.2 states that the sole amount payable by PB upon a Section 14.2 termination “shall be an early-termination fee.”

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at no more than three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is based on “Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ during the three months preceding” termination. Development Costs incurred by SFJ are not operatively defined here as fees, so the required three-month-fee cap is not established.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause makes the fee the “sole amount payable by PB” upon the relevant termination, expressly including amounts characterized as liquidated damages, and makes it in lieu of SFJ's damages claims.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because PB remains obligated to pay a termination-triggered amount that may be liquidated damages. It substantially implements the fallback's form and exclusivity requirements, but its cap uses three months of SFJ's Development Costs rather than three months' fees. The notwithstanding language generally preserves the later contingent Approval Payments, but retaining the overridden 300% and 25%-interest formulas creates avoidable interpretive friction.
